lesson.title: De la mañana a la noche
lesson.subtitle: Chaining reflexives (me levanto, me lavo, me acuesto) and time markers across a realistic day

hook.title: A Full Day in Spanish
hook.content:
Watch how reflexive verbs and stem-changing boot verbs work together across your daily routine:
• **Por la mañana me levanto a las siete** ('In the morning I get up at seven').
• **Empiezo a trabajar / estudiar a las nueve** ('I start working/studying at nine' — notice **empezar a + infinitive**!).
• **Por la noche me acuesto a las diez y duermo ocho horas** ('At night I go to bed at ten and sleep eight hours')!

pattern.title: Why 'Empezar' Always Takes 'a' Before an Infinitive
pattern.content: Just like ir a ('going to'), verbs of beginning like **empezar** ('to start/begin', e→ie boot verb: yo empiezo) always use the forward arrow **a** before a following infinitive: **Empiezo a comprender** ('I'm starting to understand'), **Empieza a hablar** ('He starts speaking')!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.german: por la mañana / por la noche

exercises.target_answer: me levanto a las siete, me acuesto, duermo ocho horas, empiezo a comprender, por la mañana / por la noche
exercises.meaning: I get up at seven, I go to bed (o→ue), I sleep eight hours (o→ue), I start to understand (e→ie + a!), in the morning / at night
exercises.explanation: Reflexives (me levanto, me acuesto) and boot verbs (empiezo, duermo) carry the daily routine.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition must link 'empezar' ('to start/begin') to a following infinitive verb?
exercises.explanation: Verbs of motion and beginning (ir a, empezar a) always take the forward arrow a before an infinitive!

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'In the morning I get up at seven'
exercises.target_answer: Por la mañana me levanto a las siete
exercises.meaning: In the morning I get up at seven
exercises.explanation: Por la mañana + me levanto + a las siete.

exercises.idea: say that you are starting to understand Spanish ('Empiezo a comprender el español')
exercises.meaning: I am starting to understand Spanish

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Por la noche me acuesto a las diez
exercises.target_answer: Por la noche me acuesto a las diez
exercises.meaning: At night I go to bed at ten
cues: I go to bed: me acuesto
exercises.explanation: Por la noche me acuesto a las diez.

summary.outcome: Chain reflexive verbs (me levanto, me acuesto), empezar a + infinitive, and time expressions across a day.

use_example.german: Por la mañana me levanto a las siete y por la noche me acuesto a las diez.
use_example.english: In the morning I get up at seven and at night I go to bed at ten.

summary.takeaway: empezar (e→ie) always takes 'a' before a following infinitive: Empiezo a comprender.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next branch ([5091] Relative Clauses in Depth): master con quien, para quien, lo que, and donde!

twist.prompt: Assemble: 'I start to eat at eight'
twist.target_answer: Empiezo a comer a las ocho
twist.explanation: Empiezo a comer a las ocho.

levantarse.english_meaning: to get up (me levanto: I get up)
levantarse.context_translation: I get up at seven o'clock.

acostarse.english_meaning: to go to bed, lie down (me acuesto: I go to bed)
acostarse.etymology_derivation: From costa ('rib/side') = 'to lay oneself on one's side'.

dormir.etymology_derivation: Latin dormīre — English dormitory and dormant.

empezar.english_meaning: to begin, to start (empiezo: I start)
empezar.shift_rule: Boot verb e → ie (takes a before infinitive)
empezar.context_phrase: La clase empieza a las nueve.
empezar.etymology_derivation: Takes a before a following infinitive: empiezo a comprender ('I'm starting to understand').

mañana.context_translation: Tomorrow I am going to work.
mañana.etymology_derivation: As an adverb (mañana) it means 'tomorrow'; as a feminine noun (la mañana) it means 'the morning' (mañana por la mañana = 'tomorrow morning')!

noche.etymology_derivation: Latin noctem. The -ct- became Spanish -ch-: octō → ocho, lactem → leche.

me.etymology_derivation: Walks left of conjugated verbs or hooks onto infinitives.
